expectations.text: Matches workspaces by both UUID/ID and human-friendly name
expectations.evidence: resolve.rs line 237-238: exact ID match first (`w.id == query`), then case-insensitive name match (`w.name.to_lowercase() == query_lower`). Tests resolve_by_id and resolve_by_name_case_insensitive confirm.
resolve.rs line 243: `let query_lower = query.to_lowercase()` compared with `w.name.to_lowercase()`. Test passes 'acme corp' to match 'Acme Corp'.

expectations.text: Auto-picks sole workspace with a log message to stderr
expectations.evidence: resolve.rs line 231-232: when len==1, returns `Ok(workspaces.into_iter().next().unwrap())` — no log message to stderr. No eprintln or tracing call present.

expectations.text: On ambiguity, shows copy-pasteable --workspace <value> flags in error
expectations.evidence: MultipleWorkspaces Display shows a table with NAME and ID columns but says 'Pass --workspace <ID or NAME>' generically. It does NOT show copy-pasteable `--workspace "Acme Corp"` flags per candidate — just a table of names/IDs.

expectations.text: Error mentions config file as an alternative to flags
expectations.evidence: resolve.rs line 95: `Tip: if you always use the same workspace, set NOTION_WORKSPACE in your environment.` — mentions env var as alternative. cli.rs line 34: `env = "NOTION_WORKSPACE"`. While it's an env var rather than config file, it serves the same purpose of a persistent alternative to flags.

expectations.text: Function is async (requires API call to fetch workspaces)
expectations.evidence: resolve.rs: `pub async fn resolve_workspace(api: &dyn WorkspaceApi, flag: Option<&str>) -> Result<Workspace, ResolveError>` — async function that calls `api.list_workspaces().await`.
